title: Winners and Sinners - August Update
snippet: We welcome new additions to the Portfolio, and two sells
content_html:
MET.L / ALTN.L / MKA.L / FMET.L / ASAI.L / IIG.L / AC8.L / VNET.L / BOOM.L / LMNZ / DLB / FTC.L

I’m now in Month 3 of my Substack journey and it has been an immense learning curve, that’s for sure.

I never intended to run a ‘portfolio’ but obliged when a number of readers suggested it, so all stocks now have BUY, WAIT / WATCH, SELL or BENCH recommendations attached to them (obviously do your own due diligence, this is just what I am doing).

Also I need to make clear the Portfolio is not exactly my own portfolio, I have stocks in my own that were purchased (and sold) in different conditions. The Wizard Portfolio here is simply constructed based on the coverage from the research, Upside and Risk/Reward calculus. As time goes on, this (Substack) Portfolio and my own will no doubt converge.

By way of further clarification, I included stocks covered in Winners pre-portfolio that I would probably have marked as WAIT/WATCH based on the charts at the time. So Performance is not quite what I would deem as satisfactory at this point of time.

Weasel clauses etc out of the way, let’s see how our Winners have been performing and what needs to happen to get into multibag territory.

Let’s start off with the Solds.

Last month saw two sales - James Cropper (a tactical sale) where management warned about adverse conditions in its high-margin hydrogen division; and Cindrigo which got the boot after doing the old smoke and mirrors trick. Details later.

So our portfolio sales look like this:

The calcs automatically deduct for 5% round trip friction, allowing for spreads / dealing costs etc; a 14.5% return so far isn’t too shabby imo.

Let’s now look at our Players on the Pitch.

The Players (Current Portfolio)

Within Wizard’s Portfolio, we are waiting for our theses to unfold, the market to realise value vs superficial optics and canned or stale narratives. We need some months for our players to be able to stretch their proverbial legs.

However I’m convinced we will see one or two multibags emerging before the end of the year, assuming no major ructions in the stock market as a whole.

Let’s run through our team updates one by one.

Metir

Read the report here

Metir had another transformative month. As you may recall the share was suspended due to the auditors dragging their heels. The FY 2025 results which duly dropped on 7th July, coinciding with the re-listing, were superb. However, management declared the need to raise £500k but note this is for growth capital plus the ‘going concern’ status flagged in the Results.

A day earlier, Alvar Financial notified that a client of theirs had discreetly upped their stake to 3.06%. Clearly word is getting out about Metir.

Then on 17th July Metir signed a Strategic MoU with Portsmouth Aviation for water monitoring in the Gulf Region. A week later, the company dropped the 10-Year Qatar CTM Project Confirmation, an absolute master-stroke in turning adversity into a long-term moat. Plus it further validates Microtox, as well as ~£30k/month or £360k/year) in high-margin recurring consumable sales across 27 CTM units, with Phase 2 expansion (17 additional units) carrying potential to increase recurring revenue past £50k/month (£600k/year). You can read the RNS here.

Alongside this CEO Bob Moore has advised us that the evaluation of Microtox by US Water giant Veralto is progressing well.

We always knew the company would need to raise; this is a sign of (accretive) growing pains, not a case of ‘keeping the lights on’.

Investors need to pinch themselves here - Metir is only a £3m mcap company - yet it’s progressing on multiple fronts and making it rain nicely for shareholders too.

The next update will probably be news of the fund-raise, but don’t be surprised if we have another, likely positive, operational update to coincide with it, given all the irons in the fire Metir has.

Flash update today - Metir is now partnering with MechLine-UK, an established, major turnkey supplier and engineering specialist that already services Thames Water, Affinity Water, Sutton & East Surrey Water, and Portsmouth Water. Bob you move too fast! :-)

Metir for me is hands-down Winner of the Month. CEO Bob Moore gets Manager of the Month. Metir remains a compelling buy.

AltynGold

Read the report here

There is not much to report on Altyn. Sekisovskoye is ticking along nicely and should be yielding higher grades now.

Everyone is waiting on permitting for the second mine, Teren-Sai. In the AGM management said they would provide an update on progress here ‘over the course of the summer.’ Let’s stay close to the RNS’s, we should receive something by Q3.

AltynGold is printing as a 4-5x at $4.4k gold - one of the highest upside producing gold miners on the market at the moment. If you are not in yet I would recommend waiting until the chart bases (the same goes for all our resource picks). When gold turns it will be game on again. You might also want to read Oak Bloke’s coverage on Altyn here.

Mkango

Read the report here

Mkango’s July 27th update announced a phased development strategy at HyProMag USA’s Texas Hub, fast-tracking the deployment of magnet cutting and finishing equipment to H1 2027 - using up to 20 tonnes of pre-processed magnet blocks imported from UK and German operations - to begin supplying U.S. commercial buyers and accelerating product qualification programs ahead of full-scale plant deployment.

This early finishing capability de-risks downstream customer relationships and establishes an immediate U.S. market presence. However it does so at the trade off of pushing back the commissioning of the fully integrated, high-margin HPMS recycling section to Q2 2028.

The core economics remain intact. Hypromag is the best (ie lowest cost and most efficient) REE patented recyling methodology on the market. Also, a serious Rare Earth supply crunch is looming (you can read here)

The Q2 Financials and Operational update will land at the end of the month. Stay tuned.

Fulcrum Metals

Read the report here

Nothing to report here, we await news of the Pilot Plant Flowsheet commissioning, expected mid-September, as well as the formalisation of the 15m Loyalist Exploration milestone shares due to the company.

ASA International

Read the report here

ASA International delivered its Q2 Update on 30th July. It demonstrated that:

  1. India is history. The company has now effectively completely derisked itself from its previously loss-making India operations. ✅

  2. Client base increased 11% y-o-y to 2.72m with Gross OLP up 17% in constant currency terms. ✅

  3. Digital Execution is on Schedule The transformation away from manual, paper-based lending is moving exactly to plan. Tanzania's digital platform is now fully live, and implementation of Temenos has now started in Kenya and Nigeria. The digital transformation boosts operating margins without affecting the benefits the company gets from its unique, high-touch lending model. ✅

So lots of positives. Guess what Mr Market fixated on?

The one small piece of news which is just a short-term blip. A minor uptick in Group PAR>30 from 2% to 2.4% caused the market to briefly throw its toys out of the pram. Note that PAR is not defaults! This blip was almost entirely driven by temporary, localised trade regulations in Uganda, not a systemic breakdown of ASA’s high-touch lending model.

ASA International is investment royalty. You are getting arguably the world’s most profitable and (best run?) financial institution at an EV/FCF of 3.3, plus a 4% yield while the market gets over itself and rerates ASA closer to where it should be.

If it were just to rerate to the much lower quality microfinance companies on the Mumbai exchange the shares would need to double. To be valued on the same level as subprime lenders they would need to triple. The valuation disconnect here is extreme.

I covered all the risks in the initiation note; from a credit risk point of view, ASA International is less risky than Western corporate credit. Facts!

This is a great entry opportunity here for anyone who is not yet invested and can see the forest from the trees (golden alleyway) in the chart below.

Intuitive Investments IIG (soon to be Acceler8 Ventures / AC8)

Read the report here

Over the past month, Intuitive Investments Group (IIG) and Acceler8 Ventures (AC8) have advanced their proposed £600 million all-share takeover. In mid-July, formal notices were issued to convene the necessary Court and General Meetings for August 3, 2026, alongside the release of the official Scheme Document and AC8’s associated prospectus. A subsequent update confirmed that if the meetings and Court Sanction Hearing on August 6 are successful, the scheme will become effective on August 13th.

That’s when we expect IIG shares to be suspended from trading on the Specialist Fund Segment on August 13th, and their listing cancelled by August 14th. The newly enlarged AC8, encompassing the IIG assets, is expected to be admitted to the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange on that date, with the newly issued shares credited to former IIG shareholders. So put that date in your diary folks!

I have been asked lots of questions about the reverse takeover. At the time of writing we see whipsawing in both companies’ stocks, this is AC8 today - up 48%:

I confess I am not well-placed to make any comment of how to ‘play’ the situation in the immediate term. Instead, I am focussed on HUI10’s rollout and progression to meeting our Free Cashflow targets and NPV, currently printing as a 5x from here on Wiz’s DCF.

If I were a gambling man, which I’m not, I would hazard a guess that we might receive an update on HUI10’s progress sometime in September. I have also been asked whether there will be institutional buying and if so when? Again, I have no idea about this, but my guess is that institutions will not move in before the end of the year at the earliest. In my view investors only need to follow the long game here, which is the digitisation of China’s state lottery.

In its last update HUI10 demonstrated parabolic adoption via its app and GTV growth but some delays on the rollout of its POS terminals and Lucky World shops. I speculated the latter may be due to the timeline of regulatory approvals from the Chinese Ministry of Finance, which are the necessary triggers to unlock the next £25 million in committed funding from Helikon.

Kudos, however, to those who sold out at IIG’s top (Johnny G your timing was impeccable!) - as to best timing to get back in, again I do not wish to guide. Well done again to management for getting this over the line.

Vianet

Read the report here

Our thesis on Vianet received a significant boost following their FY2026 audited results and recent July AGM statement. While the headline revenue growth looked anaemic (just +1.5% to £15.5m), the underlying transformation is now complete. The company has successfully navigated away from hardware dependency, with high-margin, recurring software subscriptions now generating a powerful 88% of total group turnover.

More importantly, the cash engine is now in full throttle. In FY2026, Vianet produced £4.07 million in post-working capital operating cash flow. They are now throwing off true free cash flow that has cleared their debt, flipping the balance sheet from net debt to a net cash position of £0.44 million by year-end. In a profound signal of management confidence in this new cash floor, the Board proposed an 85% hike to the total annual dividend.

Looking forward under newly appointed CEO Craig Brocklehurst, the company is showing no signs of slowing down. Management confirmed at the AGM that Q1 FY2027 trading is already ahead of expectations, with US hospitality deployments accelerating and long-term contracts providing exceptional revenue visibility. Vianet has successfully transitioned from a vulnerable hardware provider into a cash-rich, highly defensive SaaS compounder with platform economics - let’s see when the market will get the memo.

Sit tight here, don’t worry about the absence of newsflow, we just need to wait for the value to be recognised.

Next updates may be a Q2 Trading Statement in August, failing which we are due to receive Vianet’s H1 2027 results in mid-September.

Audioboom

Read the report here

I covered the Audioboom’s exceptional, blowout results last month and have nothing to add to that.

Management are doing everything right with the business yet continue to shoot themselves in the foot when it comes to presenting the Free Cashflow dynamics and the platform economics to the investment community. For some peculiar reason they steadfastly refuse, along with House Brokers Cavendish, to run numbers out past 2026 - the only company in the universe I can see failing to do that. A significant number of investors voted against the Chair and another Director at the AGM.

Of course if they were to model the numbers out further, the flywheel and delta in FCFs caused by BOOM’s operational leverage would become apparent and the valuation disconnect shown to be utterly absurd. Given that they have now been notified about the erroneous figures used by Cavendish (which they strangely sourced from other brokers) we have to wonder what’s going on there. Certainly, it seems they are going down a path of developing an adversarial relationship with shareholders, for whom it seems they have little respect.

That said it’s US midterms and CEO Stuart Last has claimed that advertising is robust, so we might see another RNS dropping with an upgrade. Warren Buffett’s quote about preferring to invest in an exceptional business with mediocre management rather than vice versa applies here.

Lastminute.com

Read the report here

Lastminute.com is another new addition to the team, added on 22nd July with H1 Results dropping just over a week later.

The market wasn’t impressed with the results, the top line was anaemic:

CEO Alessandro Petazzi referred to a softer travel market impacted by Middle East tensions. However if we look below the bonnet there’s a lot to like.

First, management is doubling down on their brand heritage by pairing a fresh marketing drive via BBH and The Romans with surging late-booking consumer demand - a sweet spot where their dynamic packages bundle distressed supplier inventory into packages commanding lucrative take rates above 12%. Look at their Google search presence from March, it has soared:

They also took the hit for the 25% headcount reduction, adding a €10.9m restructuring provision in H1 for a 25%, a structural move that permanently strips out overhead and unlocks €16m in annual recurring cash savings starting in FY27.

Third, their conversational distribution engine is already live, allowing users to query and book full package inventory directly inside ChatGPT and Claude via proprietary Model Context Protocol servers - the AI thesis I wrote about. That should start reaping rewards from Q3 on. Mr Petazzi has confirmed this ‘the second half is where the work of the first half shows up in the numbers.’ I agree with that.

Lastly, the balance sheet provides shareholders exceptional downside protection: structurally negative working capital flooded the business with summer booking deposits, driving the Net Financial Position up 197% to €94.2m - meaning net cash now backs over half the entire market cap.

Lastminute.com is an exceptional opportunity in my eyes. It is a ‘heads I win big, tails I still win’ situation. Other than a soft travel market, which the company should be able to surmount, there is nothing here not to like. I recommend reading the report if you have not already done so.

Dolby

Read the report here

Our latest buy. No sooner had we tipped it than the company dropped its Q3 results, and this happened:

Dolby’s Q3 2026 results confirm that our ‘tollbooth’ thesis is on the money. Management guided for up to $1.44 billion in revenue and 34% non-GAAP operating margins - sweet.

The architects of the open-source rebellion are capitulating, with Meta the latest to join Dolby’s Video Distribution Program, proving the absolute indispensability of Dolby's IP. Alibaba has signed on too. Moreover, management is deploying their free cash flow to authorise a massive new $350 million share repurchase programme to rapidly shrink the float.

Ultimately, this report exorcises the ‘spooks’ described in our article, cementing Dolby as a cash-gushing, high-margin software monopoly trading at an incredibly cheap valuation. This is another doozy as I see it. A gift here.

Filtronic - SHORT

Read the report here

Filtronic dropped Full Year results today and the market was unimpressed.

Filtronic has superb products - no question. But a business with superb products doth not a great investment make, especially when you are forever having to pump water into your moat just to keep it in place. You want a business where the moat needs little or no attention and from which water can be drawn (in Free Cashflows) rather than the other way around.

With Filtronic we see an object lesson of how management spins a narrative disconnected from the numbers: today they wrapped a significant decline in raw profitability inside a narrative of ‘strategic investment’ and ‘solid execution.’ They lead heavily with their custom ‘Adjusted’ metrics - we strictly ban such pyrotechnics from our methodology.

Strip away the spin and look purely at the unencumbered cash and statutory operating figures, and you can see our business analysis and bear thesis playing out in real-time. This is a capex-muncher vulnerable to delays and the whims of a single client and in my view is going to 80p.

The Subs’ Bench

We have also slowly been adding to our ‘substitute’s bench’. These are the players who may come on when conditions improve or catalysts re-establish themselves. Stay close to your Notes - when circumstances change, this is where you’ll hear first about a player ready to come onto the pitch.

In no particular order…

James Cropper - benched due to headwinds in hydrogen on the horizon flagged by management. (A tactical sell, we do love the business and the CEO is doing a great job here - this may turn on a single positive RNS).

NeoTerra - waiting for the Rare Earths serious supply deficit to come front of Mr Market’s mind.

Tekmar - waiting for the company to be able to shift into the higher margin wind energy work; their clients were hit by the Middle East ructions.

Denarius Metals - waiting for the gold market to turn. Bond yields, a strong dollar and oil prices are a triple threat and all-in-one kryptonite weighing on gold at the moment.

I will be adding to our Subs Bench over the coming weeks. These will be ‘waits’ until their respective markets / sectors / charts become constructive. If conditions change, we may see three or four subs all coming on within a couple of days. Finger on the buzzer folks :-)

Sells and Sinners

Cindrigo, which held so much promise, did a sneaky by suddenly telling us (without telling us) that the Financing Package that ‘was finalised’ yet was anything but as it has turned out.

The upshot of this is that their Kaipola ‘cash bridge’ has been burnt to cinders.

What a shame. Their German geothermal project is truly a thing of beauty, but without FCF from the Finnish Wood Pellet business to derisk the whole thing, it is now fraught with risk as the company has been thrown back onto the dreaded Funding Treadmill. You can read about it here. So Cindrigo is the Sinner of the Month.

We also sold James Cropper for reasons given above. This is purely tactical and as Arnold Schwarzenneger said, I’ll be back. You can read about the thinking process here.

Gameplan

Admittedly it may be difficult to divine a Gameplan with the Wizard’s wheeling and dealing.

I’m only two months or so in to my Substack journey and didn’t intend to add a portfolio component. Now I have done I feel an added responsibility to you, above all, not to lose money. This means maximising the vaunted 3x upside, while minimising the downside.

How am I planning to do that?

By buying cashflows. However, once a company is FreeCashFlowing it rarely offers the kind of upside we are looking for - the market has already cottoned on.

But sometimes the market is bamboozled by its own narratives and misses a stunning opportunity in plain sight. Lastminute.com in my view is one such example of an exceptional opportunity, you literally get a ‘heads I win big, tails I win not so big’ setup here.

ASA International another. Dolby another. All FCF gushers the Market is overlooking.

So per our Gameplan we have 3 Categories.

Category 1: FreeCashFlow gushers the market ignores. These are relatively safe which you can go large on. They also have net cash in the bank.

Then you have Category 2: FreeCashflow Inflecters. These are the stocks where FCFs have already inflected and the market doesn’t realise. These often offer the highest upside and safest downsides. Hardide fell into this category.

At the time of writing

  • Audioboom

  • Vianet

  • AltynGold

Then you have Category 3: Massive Free Cashflow relative to EV’ers (but in the future). These often offer insane upside. Last year this was Discovery Silver for me, 14x.

The risk of those is higher here so we need to ‘map’ the path to FCFs very carefully, ensuring they don’t get trapped in the Funding and Dilution Treadmill.

We have done this for:

  • Metir

  • Denarius Metals

  • Fulcrum Metals

  • Neoterra

  • IIG

  • Mkango

With these, investors need an aqualung. We need to go underwater with a quantified amount of oxygen before re-emerging at the boat as it is about to motor, on the basis our oxygen doesn’t run out in the interim.

This is where Wizard’s forensic and predictive computational approach to calculating Free Cashflows from the bottom up really pays off. Ofc Wiz computes the FCFs and upsides for all Categories.

Thank you all and feel free to add comments below. Stay Magical!
